## Dataset: Stable water isotopes and EC in overland flow, topsoil interflow, soil water, groundwater, and rainwater for 12 rainfall events in the Studibach catchment, Alptal, Switzerland

This dataset contains stable isotope ratios of oxygen and hydrogen &#40;O-18 and H-2&#41; and electrical conductivity &#40;EC&#41; in overland flow &#40;OF&#41;, topsoil interflow &#40;TIF&#41;, soil water, groundwater, and rainwater for 12 rainfall events during the snow-free seasons of 2021 and 2022 in the Studibach catchment, Alptal, Switzerland. <br>Overland flow, topsoil interflow &#40;i.e., lateral flow from the more densely rooted soil layer&#41;, soil water, and groundwater were collected at 14 small trenched runoff plots &#40;1 x 3 m&#41; in three subcatchments &#40;C2, C3, C5&#41; of the Studibach catchment. Overland flow was collected from the surface up to 2-5 cm depth and thus includes biomat flow. A trench was used to collect topsoil interflow &#40;up to 60 cm below the surface; see Table 1 in the manuscript for details&#41;. Rainwater was collected at two locations in the Studibach catchment &#40;in C3 and C5, respectively&#41;. Soil water was collected in between the events from suction lysimeters installed at 12.5 cm and 20 cm below the soil surface in the middle of each plot. Groundwater was collected between events from wells installed near the plots up to the soil-bedrock interface. <br>The water samples were analysed for the stable isotopes of oxygen and hydrogen &#40;O-18 and H-2&#41; using with a cavity ring-down spectroscope &#40;CRDS; L2140-i or L2130-i, Picarro, Inc., USA&#41; at the Chair of Hydrology at the University of Freiburg, Germany. The isotope ratios are reported in per mil &#40;‰&#41; relative to Vienna Standard Mean Ocean Water.<br>A more detailed description of the field setup, data collection and preparation can be found in Leuteritz et al. &#40;in press&#41;.<br>The dataset contains in addition to the sample identifier and the site and event identifiers that are used in the publication, also the sample collection date &#40;typically one day after the event&#41; and the coordinates for each plot &#40;coordinate system: WGS84&#41;. For the plots for which samples were collected with an automatic sampler &#40;ISCO&#41;, the date and time &#40;UTC&#41; of sample collection are given as well.

[View this dataset in the data catalogue](https://opendata.swiss/de/dataset/stable-water-isotopes-and-ec-in-overland-flow-topsoil-interflow-soil-water-groundwater-and-rain)

## Load packages

This template targets tidyverse (2.x) and skimr (2.x) with R 4.1 or newer for the native `|>` pipe; package versions are not pinned. Install missing packages once with `install.packages(c("tidyverse", "skimr"))`.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(skimr)
theme_set(theme_minimal())

USER_AGENT <- "OpendataSwiss-StarterCode-R/1.0"
HTTP_TIMEOUT <- 30

get_dataset <- function(url, delim = NULL, drop_empty_unnamed = TRUE, ...) {
  if (grepl("^https?://", url)) {
    local_file <- tempfile()
    on.exit(unlink(local_file), add = TRUE)
    old_options <- options(timeout = HTTP_TIMEOUT)
    on.exit(options(old_options), add = TRUE)
    status <- download.file(url, local_file, method = "libcurl", mode = "wb",
                            quiet = TRUE, headers = c("User-Agent" = USER_AGENT))
    if (status != 0) stop("Resource download failed")
    url <- local_file
  }
  data <- read_delim(url, delim = delim, show_col_types = FALSE, ...)
  stop_for_problems(data)
  if (drop_empty_unnamed && nrow(data) > 0) {
    # Blank CSV headers (often from trailing separators) become "...n".
    unnamed <- grepl("^\\.\\.\\.[0-9]+$", names(data))
    empty_unnamed <- unnamed & map_lgl(data, ~ all(is.na(.x)))
    if (any(empty_unnamed)) {
      message("Removed empty unnamed columns: ", paste(names(data)[empty_unnamed], collapse = ", "))
      data <- data[, !empty_unnamed, drop = FALSE]
    }
  }
  data
}
```

## Load data

Selected resource: **2ccec401-cf90-4e2e-a286-a75f0ec5d21e** (CSV). This notebook loads only this resource.

For CSV, the delimiter and column types are guessed. Check the preview and metadata; set `delim`, `col_types`, `na`, or `locale` in `get_dataset(...)` when needed (for example, read identifiers with leading zeros as character columns). Parsing problems stop the import so they can be addressed.

Fully empty columns named `...n` are removed on import. Named empty columns and unnamed columns containing values are kept. Use `drop_empty_unnamed = FALSE` to retain every column, including intentionally named `...n` fields.

## Missing values

```{r missing-values}
missing <- tibble(
  column = names(df),
  missing = map_int(df, ~ sum(is.na(.x))),
  missing_pct = map_dbl(df, ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100)
) |>
  arrange(desc(missing_pct))
missing

# Show up to 20 columns with missing values; percentages use all rows.
missing_plot <- missing |> filter(missing > 0) |> slice_head(n = 20)
if (nrow(missing_plot) > 0) {
  ggplot(missing_plot, aes(x = missing_pct, y = reorder(column, missing_pct))) +
    geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
    labs(x = "Missing values (%)", y = NULL, title = "Missingness by column")
} else {
  message("No missing values to plot (or the dataset has no rows).")
}
```

## Summary and distributions

`skim()` reports completeness and type-specific summaries. Inspect units before interpreting numeric codes as measurements.

```{r summary}
if (nrow(df) > 0 && ncol(df) > 0) {
  skim(df)
} else {
  message("No data to summarize.")
}
```

```{r histograms}
# Plot up to four numeric columns, excluding non-finite values only from plots.
numeric_names <- names(select(df, where(is.numeric))) |> head(4)
for (column in numeric_names) {
  values <- df[[column]]
  values <- values[is.finite(values)]
  if (length(values) > 0) {
    plot <- ggplot(tibble(value = values), aes(x = value)) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
      labs(title = column, x = column, y = "Count")
    print(plot)
  }
}
```

```{r category-counts}
# Top 10 values for up to three categorical columns, including missing values.
categorical_names <- df |>
  select(where(~ is.character(.x) || is.factor(.x) || is.logical(.x))) |>
  names() |>
  head(3)
for (column in categorical_names) {
  cat(column, "\n")
  df |> count(.data[[column]], sort = TRUE) |> head(10) |> print()
}
```
